name: Hutterites
scope: The communal Anabaptist brotherhood founded in Moravia in the 1520s-30s and named for Jakob Hutter, and the Hutterite colonies that descend from it in North America, as Britannica, The Canadian Encyclopedia and the scholarship on them (Horsch, Caldwell, Hostetler, Peter, Boldt, Pitt) describe it. Its marks in these sources are community of goods on the model of the Jerusalem church (Acts 2 and 4), adult baptism, nonresistance and opposition to war, strict separation of church and state with no part in politics, and a separate rural colony life under a council of elders. Its own texts, as the sources tie them to it, are Peter Riedemann's Rechenschaft (Account of Our Religion, Doctrine and Faith, 1540-41), which the colonies still treat as their confession of faith, and the Geschicht-Buch (the brotherhood's Chronicle). The profile represents the Hutterian Brethren as a whole; it leaves out the Bruderhof and other later groups that borrowed the name or model, and the wider Anabaptism of the Swiss Brethren and Mennonites (audited separately), and the sources on what outsiders think of Hutterites (stereotype studies) do not answer for them.

summary: The Hutterites are a communal Anabaptist brotherhood founded in Moravia in the 1520s-30s whose members hold all property in common on the model of the Jerusalem church. They practise adult baptism and nonresistance, refuse oaths and public office, and keep church and state strictly apart, while accepting civil government as ordained of God and paying taxes (but not war taxes). Their ideal is a separate, disciplined colony life of work, self-surrender and community, with men as heads of households.

notes: Themes searched in the local books (Horsch, Caldwell, Hostetler, Peter, Boldt, Pitt, Dobson): property and community of goods, government, taxes, oaths and office, nonresistance, church and state, work, marriage and women, simple living, education. Answers rest mostly on Horsch's long extracts of Riedemann's Rechenschaft and on Caldwell. The 1923 Geschicht-Buch scan's OCR is too poor for topic searches in German. Statements on economy, law and foreign policy outside these themes stay null because the sources state no position.
